mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing the unique-event constraint lets Alloy construct two distinct AuditEntries that describe the same logical event (same recording operation, same auditOp, same affectedSharee) — the structural signature of an audit log that has been mutated/duplicated, which is exactly what AppendOnly rejects.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AppendOnlyViolation { some disj ae1, ae2: AuditEntry | ae1.recordedBy = ae2.recordedBy and ae1.auditOp = ae2.auditOp and ae1.affectedSharee = ae2.affectedSharee }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing the permission-enforcement fact lets the model invent a successful operation whose (relationship, kind) is not in the permission matrix — the canonical least-privilege violation (e.g., an in-team non-related member who successfully GETs a task).
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_LeastPrivilegeViolation { some op: Operation | op.successful = BTrue and (op.effectiveRel -> op.kind) not in PermMatrix.Allowed }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing the 404-response rule frees a cross-team caller to receive a non-404 response, revealing existence of a task in another tenant — the multi-tenant information-leakage failure FR-014 is designed to block.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_LeakageViolation { some op: Operation | op.authenticated = BTrue and op.effectiveRel = RelOutsider and op.response != RespNotFound }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing the audit-per-mutation linkage lets a successful PATCH/DELETE exist with no AuditEntry — a direct violation of SC-007's 'no observable state change without an audit entry' invariant.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AuditCompletenessViolation { some op: Operation | op.successful = BTrue and op.kind = DeleteTaskKind and (no ae: AuditEntry | ae.recordedBy = op) }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing the auth gate lets an unauthenticated request flag itself as successful, which is the canonical FR-001 failure (handler runs before token introspection).
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AuthViolation { some op: Operation | op.authenticated = BFalse and op.successful = BTrue }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing the attribution fact lets the actor recorded on an AuditEntry diverge from the caller of the recording Operation — misattribution, which FR-016 forbids.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AttributionViolation { some ae: AuditEntry | ae.actor != ae.recordedBy.caller }
